input: How privacy, security, and customer‑base knowledge drive Apple to build AI models, and what limits?
expected_output: Apple builds its own AI models to protect user privacy, ensure security, and leverage deep knowledge of its customer base. By keeping models on‑device (AFM3 Core, 3 B params; AFM3 Core Advanced, 20 B params) and in the cloud (AFM3 Cloud, AFM3 Cloud Image, AFM3 Cloud Advanced), Apple can offer personalized, secure services without sending data to third‑party models. Limits include hardware constraints for large on‑device models, the need for cloud support for more complex tasks, and the ongoing challenge of balancing performance with power consumption and storage on iOS and macOS devices.

This leads to significant cost savings: 92% in SRE incident debugging, 73% in GitHub issue triage, and 47% in code waste explanation.

input: Compare LLM app deployment steps with post‑deployment monitoring, including tracing inputs/outputs and performance metrics.

Post‑deployment monitoring: 1) Trace user inputs and LLM outputs to ensure correct behavior. 2) Collect performance metrics (CPU, memory, API call count, latency). 3) Track cost and usage on the server. 4) Detect API errors and log them. 5) Use monitoring tools to alert and debug. Thus, deployment focuses on building, packaging, and releasing the app, while post‑deployment monitoring focuses on runtime observability, tracing, and performance management.
